Niemodlin Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Niemodlin, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Niemodlin only began after an 1812 Prussian tolerance edict lifted the town's prior De Non Tolerandis Judeis ban; an independent community formed September 26, 1847, reaching 84 members by 1890 before westward emigration reduced it to just 3 Jews by 1925, who soon left entirely. This cemetery, established in the first half of the 19th century beside the former synagogue, became Reich Association property in 1939 and was devastated during WWII, with destruction continuing after 1945; eyewitnesses recall tombstones surviving until the 1960s, when the site was completely destroyed. The land became private property in the 1970s; around 2019, the current owner installed an art piece featuring crosses emerging from rubble alongside symbolic graves, and rebuilt the former synagogue building as what the owner describes as an ecumenical meeting space. No memorial plaque marks the cemetery's former existence.
